这一部分先讲快速公交为什么能提高通行效率与可达性，再用乘客体验和设备故障说明设计与运行的差别，最后交代扩建计划。便利来自专用车道、提前检票和无台阶车辆等具体安排，也依赖车辆、票务和维护正常运作。

原文片段 · 1

The DART bus rapid transit (BRT) system runs on bus lanes separated from other traffic, mostly in the middle of the road to reduce stoppages. Ticket purchase and control takes place at stations prior to boarding and the buses are step-free, which means the entire route is accessible to people using wheelchairs or who are travelling with baby buggies.

专用车道与其他车辆分隔，减少公交受混合交通阻塞的机会；购票和检票放在上车之前，可以减少登车环节的拖延。无台阶车辆让轮椅使用者及推婴儿车的人更容易使用线路。accessible 在这里是实际能进入和使用，不只是知道线路在哪里。

原文片段 · 2

'The new buses are much, much better,' says Paulas George, a young IT worker. He takes the bus every day and it has cut his journey time by two-thirds. He says it is not perfect, though, complaining that drivers often refuse to turn on the air conditioning to save fuel.

乘客 Paulas 的通勤时间缩短了三分之二，但司机为节油不开空调使体验打了折扣。个人评价同时含有改善和不满，though 承接这种转折。原文描述的是这名乘客的经历，不能将相同降幅推给每一位乘客。

原文片段 · 3

That is not the only problem. A shortage of buses after a serious flood at the main depot during the rainy season means the system is carrying 200,000 people a day - half the expected capacity. Smartcards can't be used as the mechanical readers aren't working either, forcing passengers to buy individual paper tickets for every journey. Each is printed with a scannable QR code, but there are no scanners. Staff stand by the gates and tear tickets as people enter. As a result, queues are considerable at peak times.

洪水损坏车库后的车辆短缺使运量只有预期的一半；读卡器和扫码器问题又迫使乘客每次买纸票、工作人员手撕票。技术功能存在于票面或系统设计中，却未真正发挥作用，因此高峰排队明显。That 回接空调问题，说明后面还有更多运行困难。

原文片段 · 4

Morogoro Road to the north-west of the city was phase I of the BRT project. Phases II and III will install bus lanes along Nyerere Road to the south-west and Kilwa Road to the south. Construction on both routes is due to start imminently. Phase IV, towards Bagamoyo in the north, is in the preliminary design stage. 'Much of the city will have access to a world-class transport system within the space of a few years,' says Chris Kost, the Africa director of ITDP (the Institute for Transportation and Development Policy). All phases are being planned to high standards and, once complete, a third of city residents will be within a short walk of the BRT network.

叙述从当前故障转向分期扩建：第一期已有线路，第二、三期即将施工，第四期尚在初步设计。完成后约三分之一居民能步行短距离接入网络，是带条件的未来覆盖描述。不同阶段不能都理解成已经建好并投入使用。

词语与搭配

prior to boarding

在上车之前

prior to 比 before 稍正式；to 是介词，后接 boarding，说明购票检票发生的顺序。

accessible to people using wheelchairs

轮椅使用者能够使用

be accessible to 指对某群体可进入、可使用；这里有无台阶设计作为具体支撑。

half the expected capacity

预期运载能力的一半

expected 标明比较基准是预期值，不是原有实际客流量。

within a short walk of

在步行很短距离即可到达……的范围内

常用来描述住宅与车站、服务设施的接近程度；原文用于尚待完成的线路网络。

句子精读

Ticket purchase and control takes place at stations prior to boarding and the buses are step-free, which means the entire route is accessible to people using wheelchairs or who are travelling with baby buggies.

购票和检票都在乘客上车前于车站进行，而且公交车没有台阶，这意味着轮椅使用者或推着婴儿车出行的人都能使用整条线路。

control 在票务语境中是检票。and 连接车站流程与车辆设计，which means 引出无障碍结果。using wheelchairs 和 who are travelling with baby buggies 都修饰 people，分别列出受益人群；引文保留原文形式。

All phases are being planned to high standards and, once complete, a third of city residents will be within a short walk of the BRT network.

各期工程都正在按照高标准规划；待工程完成后，全市三分之一的居民步行很短距离就能到达快速公交网络。

are being planned 表示正在规划。once complete 是省略结构，意思是这些建设完成以后，并不修饰居民。will be 与 once 一起把覆盖率限定为未来完工后的状态。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

accessible to people using wheelchairs

便于轮椅使用者使用

用于说明公共交通替代方案应照顾不同乘客；需配合无台阶入口、站台等具体设计。

用于写作：交通题中的替代方式不只是增加车辆，还包括让不同人群能实际使用。

within a short walk of

距……很近，步行即可到达

说明住房与公交网络的空间联系；是否足够近应由实际布局支持。

用于写作：直接用于比较高层住宅的条件：密度优势需要交通可达性支持。 · 用于写作：说明公交替代汽车所需的接近性与可靠性，连接设施安排和出行选择。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。
Rethinking the Past · 渐进变化与性别预设未作答选择题 / 句尾匹配 · 4 段 · 365 词 · 5 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 70 页

按原题号作答。保留考试原文与题目难度；以下是连续原段裁切，未改写原文。

原第6–9段连续裁切；题面sixth/seventh/final paragraph分别对应本片段第1/2/4段。匹配题完整保留A–F。

原文片段 · 1In a sense, we shouldn't be surprised that so many of these behaviours had their origins in older, extinct hominins. Evolution usually works by incremental steps and so does technology. The first birds weren't great at flying, and the first mobile phones weren't great at, well, anything really. The idea that there was a sudden explosion of intelligence and creativity at some point in our evolution isn't inherently ridiculous: sometimes a system hits a tipping point and undergoes runaway change. But there was never that much evidence that human evolution worked this way. Instead, it seems the Neanderthals and many others all walked so we could run.

原文片段 · 2One way or another, the H. naledi story is going to be an example of letting our preconceptions get in the way of the evidence. The same is true for our ideas about gender in prehistory. Archaeology was invented by individuals with now unfashionably patriarchal views about gender, and those notions fed into their research. Today's researchers are trying to unpick this stuff, and there have been some significant steps in recent years.

原文片段 · 3Perhaps the most dramatic was the demolition of 'Man the Hunter'. This was the idea, promoted for decades, that in most prehistoric societies the men went out to hunt and the women looked after the home. However, a meta-analysis published in June 2023 compiled data on several dozen foraging societies and found women hunted in 80 per cent of them. In line with this, it emerged that an ancient spear-throwing tool called an atlatl enables women to launch projectiles at the same speed as men. We have also seen growing evidence of women occupying positions of authority in ancient societies. The Viking queen Thyra may have helped unify Denmark in the 900s. Going further back, an Iberian leader from around 4000 years ago turned out to be female, not male as many had assumed, when proteins in her teeth were analysed.

原文片段 · 4It seems that the more we find out about past societies, the more our preconceptions about the ways society 'has to be' turn out to be wrong. Inequality, authoritarianism and patriarchy aren't inevitable. They're choices, and prehistory shows us that we can choose differently.

共用选项 · 原题 33、34

  • A. Homo sapiens emerged at an earlier point in time than experts previously believed.
  • B. previous assumptions about who had power in the prehistoric world were inaccurate.
  • C. gender roles in extinct hominin species were different from those in Homo sapiens societies.
  • D. experts may have been mistaken about who looked for food in early human communities.
  • E. Homo sapiens was probably not the only species capable of sophisticated workmanship.
  • F. other species managed to survive in harsh environments before the arrival of Homo sapiens.

28. In the sixth paragraph, the writer mentions mobile phones to make the point that

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

  • A. most developments happen in a gradual way.
  • B. innovation can come from a variety of sources.
  • C. not all technological advancements are positive.
  • D. the path of evolution can often be unpredictable.

29. In the seventh paragraph, the phrase 'unpick this stuff' refers to the task of

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

  • A. assessing the impact of certain recent research findings.
  • B. questioning the authenticity of evidence used in earlier research.
  • C. conducting research into how prehistoric societies were organised.
  • D. reevaluating research influenced by outdated beliefs about society.

30. What does the writer suggest in the final paragraph?

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

  • A. Studying past societies could help us create a fairer society today.
  • B. We should not judge past societies by the standards of modern society.
  • C. We still have much to learn about how societies have evolved over history.
  • D. There is more than one way to interpret evidence about societies in prehistoric times.

33. An academic publication from June 2023 shows that

Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A–F, below.

34. Analysis of a 4000-year-old Iberian leader indicates that

Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A–F, below.

对照答案，回到证据

第 28 题 · A

手机比喻说明技术和进化多为逐步发展；并非评价当代手机好坏。

Evolution usually works by incremental steps and so does technology.

第 29 题 · D

this stuff回指旧父权观念渗入研究，需要重新评估受这些观念影响的研究；不是指证据造假。

Archaeology was invented by individuals with ... patriarchal views ... those notions fed into their research. Today's researchers are trying to unpick this stuff

第 30 题 · A

考察史前社会揭示当代制度并非必然，支持我们选择更公平社会。作者不是仅说仍有未知。

Inequality, authoritarianism and patriarchy aren't inevitable. They're choices, and prehistory shows us that we can choose differently.

第 33 题 · D

新汇总反驳男性负责狩猎的旧假定；D谁找食物，B谁掌权不能互换。

a meta-analysis published in June 2023 ... found women hunted in 80 per cent of them

第 34 题 · B

牙齿蛋白分析推翻领导者为男性的假设，对应谁有权力的旧看法不准确。

an Iberian leader ... turned out to be female, not male as many had assumed

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

作者从渐进演化谈到研究预设，再用女性狩猎和担任领导者的材料质疑单一的史前性别分工故事。结尾由历史认识上升到对社会选择的评论，这是作者的论述立场，不应把它当作所有史前社会相同的证明。

原文片段 · 1

In a sense, we shouldn't be surprised that so many of these behaviours had their origins in older, extinct hominins. Evolution usually works by incremental steps and so does technology. The first birds weren't great at flying, and the first mobile phones weren't great at, well, anything really. The idea that there was a sudden explosion of intelligence and creativity at some point in our evolution isn't inherently ridiculous: sometimes a system hits a tipping point and undergoes runaway change. But there was never that much evidence that human evolution worked this way. Instead, it seems the Neanderthals and many others all walked so we could run.

鸟类飞行与早期手机的类比说明复杂能力往往逐步积累。作者承认系统可能达到临界点后迅速变化，但认为人类演化突然发生智力爆发的证据并不充分。walked so we could run 是比喻：早期人族积累的能力为后来发展铺路，不是字面上的走路与跑步史。

原文片段 · 2

One way or another, the H. naledi story is going to be an example of letting our preconceptions get in the way of the evidence. The same is true for our ideas about gender in prehistory. Archaeology was invented by individuals with now unfashionably patriarchal views about gender, and those notions fed into their research. Today's researchers are trying to unpick this stuff, and there have been some significant steps in recent years.

不论 Homo naledi 的争议最后如何解决，作者都认为这反映预设可能妨碍理解证据。随后把同一问题转到性别研究：早期考古学家的父权观念进入研究解释，如今的研究者尝试把这些观念从材料中拆解出来。those notions 回指前面的性别观念。

原文片段 · 3

Perhaps the most dramatic was the demolition of 'Man the Hunter'. This was the idea, promoted for decades, that in most prehistoric societies the men went out to hunt and the women looked after the home. However, a meta-analysis published in June 2023 compiled data on several dozen foraging societies and found women hunted in 80 per cent of them. In line with this, it emerged that an ancient spear-throwing tool called an atlatl enables women to launch projectiles at the same speed as men. We have also seen growing evidence of women occupying positions of authority in ancient societies. The Viking queen Thyra may have helped unify Denmark in the 900s. Going further back, an Iberian leader from around 4000 years ago turned out to be female, not male as many had assumed, when proteins in her teeth were analysed.

多个例子从不同方向松动男性狩猎、女性留家的单一故事：对数十个采集狩猎社会的汇总发现多数有女性狩猎，投矛工具可缩小投射速度差别，古代女性领导者也有新的证据。80%是这份分析涉及的社会比例，不能扩展为所有史前社会；Thyra 的作用仍以 may 表示可能。

原文片段 · 4

It seems that the more we find out about past societies, the more our preconceptions about the ways society 'has to be' turn out to be wrong. Inequality, authoritarianism and patriarchy aren't inevitable. They're choices, and prehistory shows us that we can choose differently.

作者认为，越了解过去，就越能看到今天视为理所当然的社会安排并非唯一可能。把不平等、威权和父权称为 choices 是结尾的价值判断，作用是拓展读者对社会的想象，而不是声称过去所有社会都平等或自由。

词语与搭配

incremental steps

逐步累积的小幅变化

incremental 强调累积过程；与突然的爆发式变化形成对照。

hits a tipping point

达到临界点

比喻系统发生转折的阈值，文中承认这种机制可能存在，却未断言人类演化必然如此。

get in the way of the evidence

妨碍正确看待证据

get in the way of 表示阻碍；主语是 preconceptions，指先入为主的观念影响解释。

occupying positions of authority

担任有权威的职位

指在社会中拥有领导或决策地位，比简单说某个人受到尊敬更具体。

句子精读

The idea that there was a sudden explosion of intelligence and creativity at some point in our evolution isn't inherently ridiculous: sometimes a system hits a tipping point and undergoes runaway change.

认为人类演化过程中某个时点曾突然出现智力与创造力的爆发，这种想法本身并不荒谬：有时系统确实会达到临界点，并经历迅速扩大的变化。

that 从句说明 idea 的具体内容。isn't inherently ridiculous 是有限度的认可，并不等于作者接受这个历史解释。冒号后的系统变化说明其理论上可想象；后文再转向实际证据不足。

Going further back, an Iberian leader from around 4000 years ago turned out to be female, not male as many had assumed, when proteins in her teeth were analysed.

再往更早的年代看，约四千年前的一位伊比利亚领导者，在牙齿中的蛋白质被分析后，被发现是女性，而非许多人此前以为的男性。

Going further back 提示叙述时间继续向前追溯。turned out to be 表示后来查明的事实；as many had assumed 插入先前的认识。when 从句交代认识改变所依赖的分析情境，her 回指这位领导者。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。
Water hyacinth · 入侵植物与能源问题未作答事实判断 TFNG · 4 段 · 407 词 · 7 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 82 页

按原题号作答。保留考试原文与题目难度；以下是连续原段裁切，未改写原文。

开篇连续4段保留完整因果背景；两道NG另核对了全文，没有把片段未出现的内容当答案。健康数值只作为原考试文章陈述理解。

原文片段 · 1Water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes), an aquatic plant native to South America, first appeared in countries in Africa in the early 1900s. Scientists there called it the 'world's worst aquatic weed', after it spread from the southernmost tip of Africa in the early 1900s and started obstructing major dams and rivers.

原文片段 · 2In east Africa the plant arrived with Belgian colonists in Rwanda, who liked the look of its glossy leaves and delicate purple flowers floating in their ponds. But by the 1980s, it had 'escaped' out of the country via the Kagera river and made its way downstream to Lake Victoria. There, with no natural predators and perfect temperature conditions, the plant began spreading in the open water, blocking fishing routes and providing a new habitat for disease-carrying mosquitoes.

原文片段 · 3For the women who smoke fish from the lake to sell it has meant declining income, as the boats that once brought the fish to shore by the hundreds struggle to navigate through the mass of plants. But water hyacinth isn't their only headache. In order to smoke the fish that they buy, they must gather huge quantities of firewood, sometimes walking as far as 10km each way to collect enough to complete their work. And each day as they cook, they breathe in the thick, grey smoke. About three out of four families in Kenya depend on wood or charcoal to cook their daily meals, and the rate is even higher in rural areas, Kenya's latest demographic and health survey shows. Using solid fuels like these for cooking increases indoor pollution. The World Health Organization estimates that about 14,300 Kenyans die annually as a result of indoor air pollution - most of which is caused by cooking and heating sources.

原文片段 · 4Some years ago, on the shores of Lake Victoria, huge piles of water hyacinth that villagers had taken out of the water in an attempt to clear it were a common sight. But buried in those decaying waxy leaves was a renewable energy gold mine. It turns out the floating plant isn't just good at spreading - its foliage also contains a high ratio of carbon to nitrogen. It's a magic combination that has captivated researchers' imaginations since as early as the 1980s when, across the world, they began to explore its potential as a biofuel. Just about 4kg of the dried plant would be enough to cater for a large family's daily energy needs, early research predicted.

1. Water hyacinth was introduced as a decorative plant in east Africa.

2. Fishermen took some water hyacinth plants to Lake Victoria.

Do the following statements agree with the information given in the reading passage? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

3. It is now difficult to force boats through the thick water hyacinth on Lake Victoria.

Do the following statements agree with the information given in the reading passage? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

4. Chemicals produced by the water hyacinth plants are affecting the numbers of fish in Lake Victoria.

Do the following statements agree with the information given in the reading passage? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

5. Cooking with charcoal has been proved to be even worse for people's health than cooking with wood.

Do the following statements agree with the information given in the reading passage? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

6. People found it impossible to remove much water hyacinth from Lake Victoria.

Do the following statements agree with the information given in the reading passage? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

7. Scientists started investigating the possibility of using water hyacinth to generate biogas in the last century.

Do the following statements agree with the information given in the reading passage? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

对照答案，回到证据

第 1 题 · TRUE

liked the look与自家池塘花叶说明最初作装饰用途。

Belgian colonists in Rwanda, who liked the look of its glossy leaves and delicate purple flowers floating in their ponds

第 2 题 · FALSE

实际传播路径是河流顺流而下，不是渔民运送。

it had 'escaped' out of the country via the Kagera river and made its way downstream to Lake Victoria

第 3 题 · TRUE

struggle to navigate对应difficult to force boats through。

the boats ... struggle to navigate through the mass of plants

第 4 题 · NOT GIVEN

文中说堵住捕鱼线路并供蚊子栖息，没有说植物产生化学物质影响鱼数；渔获难运不等于鱼类减少。

blocking fishing routes and providing a new habitat for disease-carrying mosquitoes

第 5 题 · NOT GIVEN

原文并列木材与木炭作为有害固体燃料，但全文没有健康危害高低比较。

About three out of four families in Kenya depend on wood or charcoal ... Using solid fuels like these ... increases indoor pollution

第 6 题 · FALSE

huge piles与taken out说明已移除大量植物，直接反驳impossible to remove much。

huge piles of water hyacinth that villagers had taken out of the water ... were a common sight

第 7 题 · TRUE

1980s属于20世纪；题面last century对应原文年代，不要求你查当今研究。

since as early as the 1980s ... began to explore its potential as a biofuel

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

文章从水葫芦的入侵路径写到渔业收入、做饭燃料和室内烟尘，再把同一种植物转看为潜在能源。两类问题由湖边家庭的生活相连，结尾的能源价值仍是研究和预测所提出的潜力。

原文片段 · 1

Water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes), an aquatic plant native to South America, first appeared in countries in Africa in the early 1900s. Scientists there called it the 'world's worst aquatic weed', after it spread from the southernmost tip of Africa in the early 1900s and started obstructing major dams and rivers.

水葫芦原产南美，20世纪初进入非洲并开始堵塞重要水坝和河道。aquatic 表示水生；weed 在这里体现它在当地环境中的妨碍作用。最糟糕的水生杂草是文中科学家的称呼，具有评价色彩。

原文片段 · 2

In east Africa the plant arrived with Belgian colonists in Rwanda, who liked the look of its glossy leaves and delicate purple flowers floating in their ponds. But by the 1980s, it had 'escaped' out of the country via the Kagera river and made its way downstream to Lake Victoria. There, with no natural predators and perfect temperature conditions, the plant began spreading in the open water, blocking fishing routes and providing a new habitat for disease-carrying mosquitoes.

它最初作为观赏植物进入卢旺达池塘，随后顺河进入维多利亚湖。缺少天敌且温度适宜，使其迅速扩散：既阻碍捕鱼路线，也为携病蚊虫提供栖息地。escaped 带引号，把植物离开受控种植环境写成逃出。

原文片段 · 3
